plain_text:
Montalegre Bernstein became well known
for both her political activism and her role
as the fashionable social nucleus of the
Bernstein household.

plain_text:
In a letter addressed to Bernstein sometime
early in their relationship, she speaks plainly
about his love affairs with men and wonders
if he might be willing to try marriage another
way. She writes,
“... let’s try and see what
happens if you are free to do as you like, but
without guilt and confession, please!”

“I am willing to accept you as you

myself to the L.B. altar... I happen to love
you very much.

relationship. By all accounts, the marriage

plain_text:
The filmmakers may only guess at what
was really said between them in the halls of
their Manhattan apartment, or the wounds
a life of hidden loves could leave on two
people. But a symphony is incomplete
without its changing movements, and a long
relationship perhaps impossible without its
own transformations.
